problem: Reactive policies trained on a small set of maps fail to generalize zero-shot to novel map layouts and goal locations; planning agents are hard to train efficiently across many layouts.
motivation: Humans can navigate by reading a paper map, which suggests an agent should be able to use an abstract 2-D occupancy map (treated as an image) to navigate unseen environments. Model-based navigation separates map layout from goal location and enables longer-horizon planning, so it should transfer better than reactive policies when few training maps are available.
key_idea: Learn a hypermodel that reads an abstract 2-D map and goal to generate a planning model, trained by aligning its predictions with real trajectories from multi-task off-policy data and by n-step goal relabelling to give planners denser feedback.
insight: Only the abstract is available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract claims that disentangling map layout from goal location, together with model-based planning, transfers better to novel maps and goals than reactive policies. Trajectory-alignment training and n-step goal relabelling are presented as the ingredients that make learning efficient from few training maps.
method: Hypermodel: a network that takes an abstract 2-D occupancy map (as an image) and produces a planning model, capturing patterns from a limited number of maps and goals.
Trajectory alignment: maximizes agreement between hypermodel predictions and real trajectories, extracting information from multi-task off-policy experience.
n-step goal relabelling: relabels goals in collected trajectories to construct denser feedback for the planner.
Model-based planning: a planner uses the generated model for longer-term planning at novel locations, in contrast to reactive policies.

setting.backbone: learned hypermodel + planner (details not given in abstract)
setting.training_data: DeepMind Lab environments with layouts from a small proportion of training maps; off-policy multi-task experience
setting.observation: abstract 2-D occupancy map given as an image, plus goal location (agent observation details not stated)
setting.privileged: an abstract 2-D occupancy map of the test environment is given as input

results: The abstract claims superior zero-shot transfer to novel maps and goals in DeepMind Lab, but gives no numbers or named baselines.
limitations: Evaluated only in DeepMind Lab layouts (per the abstract)
Requires an abstract 2-D occupancy map of the test environment at test time
